title: Learning Options for Compositional Motor Control with Adapter Banks
summary: The method replaces monolithic multitask policies (a task-conditioned recurrent controller) with a shared recurrent core modulated by discrete, adapter-like low-rank perturbations that a frozen high-level policy sequences into novel movements. The cost is training a closed-loop biomechanical control stack end-to-end plus a discrete latent selection mechanism, which is a research training pipeline rather than an inference-time optimization. It can fail when the target domain is not closed-loop motor control: the discrete option structure and emergent low-rank subspaces are demonstrated only in biomechanical simulation, and the claim does not transfer to language, vision, or general production ML workloads.
rationale: The technique addresses compositional motor control in biomechanical simulation, which falls outside the reader's LLM-focused production scope and offers no adoptable component for their inference or training constraints.
technique: Adapter banks over shared recurrent core for motor control

The cost is training a closed-loop biomechanical control stack end-to-end plus a discrete latent selection mechanism, which is a research training pipeline rather than an inference-time optimization. It can fail when the target domain is not closed-loop motor control: the discrete option structure and emergent low-rank subspaces are demonstrated only in biomechanical simulation, and the claim does not transfer to language, vision, or general production ML workloads.
Up to an order-of-magnitude lower generalization error than a task-input-conditioned multitask baseline on novel closed-loop motor sequences, with a frozen-core high-level policy.
